title: Over 1.8 billion trees mapped in Africa’s drylands
summary: Analysis of high-resolution images located and measured the crowns of over 1.8 billion trees across 1.3 million km² of West Africa. Validation used manual annotations and field data; the study counts trees but does not yet measure their stored carbon.

evidence.tested: Tree detections checked against manually annotated data and field data from the region; the abstract itself does not describe the validation method.
evidence.unknown: The study counts trees but does not yet measure stored carbon; the method can mistake stones for trees and gets harder with more detail.
evidence.ai_role: Deep learning (fully convolutional network trained on about 90,000 hand-marked trees) on submetre satellite imagery mapped the crowns of over 1.8 billion trees.
